title: delta-stable-toolcall-migration-and-sdk-ergonomics-wip
content:
Context:
This is an exploratory PRD for a migration path we can offer customers who currently rely on monolithic, synchronous tool-call semantics to a delta-driven streaming surface that preserves deterministic tool semantics while improving latency, bandwidth efficiency, and SDK ergonomics.

Status and intent:
- Draft / exploration: this doc surfaces the high-level UX and compatibility constraints we need for a safe migration.
- Goal: ship an incremental migration (beta) that supports both: a) existing blocking tool-call semantics (compat layer) and b) a new delta-stable streaming-first API that native SDKs can adopt.

Problem statement:
- Many customers build workflows where the model triggers external tool calls (search, code execution, DB writes). Current hosted API streaming surfaces either: always stream model tokens or provide an opaque tool call event with a blocking wait.
- Blocking waits cause tail latency and reduce throughput. Fully non-blocking streaming with partial outputs works for free-form text but is hazardous for tool calls requiring idempotency, ordering, or explicit commit semantics.
- SDK ergonomics are the gating factor: engineering teams prefer a small number of clear patterns (call-sync, call-async-with-callback, call-transaction) with explicit fallbacks.

Key requirements (high level):
1) Backwards compatibility: existing synchronous tool-call behavior should be re-creatable with minimal code changes.
2) Deterministic migration: client-side replay and server-side idempotency keys must enable repeatable tool execution when resuming streams or re-sending requests.
3) Delta stability: clients should receive incremental structured deltas (frames) that can be merged deterministically to produce the same final tool input/state as the blocking path.
4) Telemetry & observability: token-level cost/latency tagging, tool-call lineage, and per-call success/failure codes surfaced in Console.
5) Performance: the new streaming path should reduce median end-to-end latency for typical tool-call flows by 25–40% in our benchmarks.
6) Security: allow customers to opt for a strict private-control-plane mode for tool invocation metadata (no payload logged in hosted control plane).

Constraints and guardrails:
- Tool calls with side effects require an explicit commit phase. Streaming deltas should never implicitly commit side-effects without a clear commit signal.
- SDKs must default to safe semantics (no speculative commit) and expose ergonomics to opt into speculative local rendering or prefetching.
- We must support large payloads (>1MB) as attachments referenced by IDs to avoid long token sequences in streams.

Proposed surface (conceptual):
- Delta Frames: small JSON-LD like frames emitted over the stream indicating: partial_text (optional), tool_intent (structured), tool_inputs (partial), tool_call_id (stable id), markers ("checkpoint", "commit_request", "commit_confirm", "abort").
- Meta-handshake: initial response includes a handshake frame listing: server_capabilities (delta-stable, resumable), idempotency_token_hint, preferred_frame_size, streaming_version.
- Tool-call lifecycle:
  1) intent_frame: model expresses an intent (tool name + structured args schema id)
  2) input_frames: optional incremental input frames for the tool payload
  3) precommit_checkpoint: SDK receives a checkpoint frame with checksum and resume cursor; client may persist locally
  4) commit_request: client can request an explicit server-side commit (sync) or indicate "commit-later" to pass commit responsibility to a separate transaction service
  5) commit_confirm / abort: final server-side frame acknowledging commit or describing an actionable error

SDK ergonomics (recommendations):
- High-level SDK patterns (JS/Go/Python):
  * syncInvoke(tool, args): blocks until commit_confirm or an error. (Compatibility wrapper around streaming lifecycle.)
  * streamInvoke(tool, args, onFrame): returns a stream handle; onFrame receives delta frames, checkpoints, and optional partial outputs. Client must call commit(handle) to finalize side-effects.
  * transactionalInvoke(tool, args, txnOptions): wraps multiple tool calls under a client-managed transaction id; server provides atomic commit semantics when available.

- Default behavior and safety:
  * By default, SDKs will buffer tool_inputs until a precommit_checkpoint arrives before returning anything to the caller that could be used to drive side-effects locally.
  * SpeculativeLocalRender: opt-in flag where SDK exposes partial tool outputs for UI responsiveness while marking them as speculative until commit_confirm. Useful for mobile UX. Requires clear toggle and telemetry flagging.

Operational and backend changes (overview):
- Router: must carry streaming-version and prefer routes capable of providing delta-stable frames (dedicated vs hosted).
- Serving runtime: support atomic partial persistence for tool payload checkpoints and a lightweight resume protocol (cursor + checksum).
- Telemetry: extend traces to include tool_call_id and checkpoint cursors. Console: new per-call timeline view showing frames and commit states.
- Billing: metricize frames vs tokens; charging model must be transparent — preliminary idea: base per-token charge + fixed per-tool-call commit fee.

Compatibility and migration plan:
Phase 0 — internal SDK alpha (1–2 sprints):
- Implement streaming protocol parser in SDKs, opt-in flag in hosted-api request. Basic commit/abort APIs.
- Internal tests: simulate flaky networks and resume semantics.

Phase 1 — limited beta (4–6 sprints):
- Beta customers (developer tools and automation teams) run a dual-path: continue using syncInvoke but optionally enable streamInvoke to test latency benefits.
- Metrics to validate: median end-to-end latency, number of resumed calls, speculative rendering adoption, incidence of double-commits.

Phase 2 — general availability (GA):
- Default to streaming path for new SDK clients. Provide migration helper that wraps old sync calls via syncInvoke.
- Announce pricing model and console telemetry.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Latency: 25–40% reduction in median E2E latency for tool-invocation-heavy workloads.
- Safety: <0.01% double-commit rate in beta.
- Adoption: X% of active API keys using streaming toolcall within 3 months of GA.
- Developer satisfaction: qualitative feedback via pilot interviews; target 4.2/5 in SDK ergonomics survey.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we surface partial failures for multi-tool transactions? Do we provide a server-side compensating action framework or merely signals for clients to implement compensation?
- Pricing: how to fairly bill for long-lived streams vs large attached payloads? Need Finance input (JIRA: PROD-3421).
- Interoperability with Private deployments where audit/logging rules mandate no hosted persistence of payloads; must implement a "control-plane-stripped" mode.
- Security classification for speculative rendering: ensure we surface disclaimers and opt-in flags to customers that might inadvertently present uncommitted outputs.

Implementation notes and engineering TODOs (rough):
- [ENG-frontend] define wire-format for delta frames and handshake (draft JSON schema).
- [SDK] implement stream parser, commit/abort wrappers, and forward-compat tests. Add flag: prefer_delta_streaming=true.
- [Router] routing policy extension: prefer-streaming-capable nodes; fallback to sync routing when unavailable.
- [Console] timeline UI: per-call frames, with ability to expand checkpoints and view payload diffs.
- [Privacy] add control-plane-stripped request header; ensure audit docs updated.
- [QA] chaos tests for resumes, duplicate commits, and partial payloads.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally mixes product goals, rough protocol ideas, and SDK patterns. Looking for feedback on the following specifically:
  1) Are the proposed commit lifecycle signals sufficient for common integrations (search, code-exec, DB writes)?
  2) Should we provide server-side transaction primitives or keep transactions a client responsibility?
  3) Pricing model preferences (per-commit fee vs per-frame): what would Sales/Finance advise for early adopters?

Related tickets and references:
- PROD-3421 (migration/pricing)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pulls/768 (protocol draft)
- Slack thread: #hosted-api-streaming (links: invite-only)

Quick sketch (example stream sequence):
- handshake frame: {"streaming_version":"v2-delta", "idempotency_hint":"abc-123"}
- intent_frame: {"tool":"search", "schema":"search-v1", "tool_call_id":"tc-1001"}
- input_frame (partial): {"tool_call_id":"tc-1001","fields":{"q":"how to reduce token cost"}}
- precommit_checkpoint: {"tool_call_id":"tc-1001","cursor":"c-42","checksum":"sha256:..."}
- partial_text: {"tool_call_id":"tc-1001","partial":"Found 3 results..."}
- commit_request (client): {"tool_call_id":"tc-1001","commit":"now"}
- commit_confirm: {"tool_call_id":"tc-1001","status":"ok","result_ref":"res-77"}

Rough UX example in JS (SDK):
- const handle = await client.streamInvoke('search', {q: 'x'});
- handle.on('frame', f => { if (f.type === 'partial_text') render(f.partial); if (f.type === 'checkpoint') persist(f.cursor); });
- await handle.commit(); // waits for commit_confirm

Appendix: rough proto (informal)
- Frame envelope: {"type":"<intent|input|checkpoint|partial_text|commit_confirm|abort>", "tool_call_id":"...", "payload":{...}}
- Resumption: resume(header:{tool_call_id, cursor, checksum}) -> server resumes stream from next frame if checksum matches.

-- end of draft --

Ava: ping me with feedback on commit lifecycle and SDK patterns. Will iterate into a tighter PRD once we align on server transaction primitives and pricing guidance.
